about.title: About and contact
about.first: I am Agustin Argüello, a developer focused on building useful, efficient, and maintainable software. I enjoy creating complete solutions, from databases and backend services to the final interface, combining technical thinking with a practical product perspective.
about.second: I work especially with web technologies, desktop systems, Linux servers, databases, and tools designed to solve real problems.

hero.copy: A memory game developed in Assembly 8086 for emu8086. It recreates Simon Says with a text-mode interface, colored regions through BIOS INT 10h video services, mouse input, levels, progressive difficulty, scoring, and complete win or loss screens.

summary.title: What it demonstrates
summary.copy: It is more than a game: it shows control of virtual hardware, execution flow, game state, and UI without modern libraries.

memory.title: Memory sequences
memory.copy: The program generates a color sequence, displays it to the player, and validates every click against the expected position in the round.

input.title: Mouse interaction
input.copy: It detects clicks and coordinates to determine whether the user pressed the gray, blue, red, or green quadrant.

levels.title: Levels and difficulty
levels.copy: It manages score, level, easy/medium/hard difficulty, and an automatic mode that adjusts the speed during play.

tech.title: Technical highlights
tech.copy: The project solves an interactive experience with resources close to the system, prioritizing text mode for performance over pixel-by-pixel graphics in emu8086.

interrupts.title: System interrupts
interrupts.copy: It uses BIOS and DOS services to build the text-mode screen, move the cursor, print text, read time, wait, and control the mouse.

macros.title: Reusable macros
macros.copy: It defines macros to paint regions, move the cursor, and print repeated characters, reducing repetition across screens.

textUi.title: Text-mode UI
textUi.copy: It builds complete text-mode screens with colored rectangles, centered messages, a loading view, a difficulty menu, and the game board, avoiding pixel-by-pixel graphics.

random.title: Pseudorandom generation
random.copy: It builds sequences from time, seeds, and arithmetic operations to produce values that represent colors.

code.title: Representative excerpt
code.copy: The macros show how repeated text-mode interface operations are abstracted: painting regions, moving the cursor, and reusing BIOS video services without drawing individual pixels.

constraints.title: Designing with constraints
constraints.copy: Creating a playable interface without HTML, CSS, canvas, or libraries requires thinking in text-mode coordinates, regions, color attributes, and screen flow.

state.title: Managing state manually
state.copy: The game requires managing arrays, indices, difficulty, sequences, attempts, score, and resets without high-level structures.

maintainable.title: Writing maintainable ASM
maintainable.copy: The next step would be extracting constants with EQU, organizing routines more clearly, and taking greater care with push/pop symmetry for robustness.

hero.copy: Technical material about lossless Huffman compression: frequencies, a heap, binary tree, code table, bit handling, and reconstruction during decompression.

summary.title: What it demonstrates
summary.copy: The page explains how a data structure can become a real compressed file, moving from tree theory down to bit manipulation.

tree.title: Huffman tree
tree.copy: Building a binary tree from frequencies by combining the lightest nodes until one root remains.

heap.title: Priority queue
heap.copy: Using a heap to efficiently extract the nodes with the lowest frequency during tree construction.

bits.title: Bit manipulation
bits.copy: An explanation of shifts, masks, OR, and AND operations to write compact sequences.

bitfield.title: Bitfield: low-level operations and bit arithmetic
bitfield.intro: In many compression algorithms, such as Huffman, storing complete characters is not enough. Making better use of space requires writing variable-length codes, which means manipulating data at the bit level.
bitfield.definition: A bitfield is a structure that stores a sequence of bits in a numeric value together with a length counter. Its basic operation, bits_agregar, appends a new bit to the field.
bitfield.addTitle: Adding a bit with shifting and OR
bitfield.addCopy: Suppose the structure contains 12 bits and we want to add a 1. First its size is increased, then a mask is created by shifting 1 to the correct position.
bitfield.zeroCopy: When the bit to add is 0, the numeric value usually does not need to change because new positions are assumed to be zero; only tamano is updated.

algorithm.title: What is the Huffman algorithm?
algorithm.intro: Huffman is a lossless compression method that assigns variable-length codes: more frequent symbols receive shorter codes, while less frequent ones receive longer codes.
algorithm.copy: Its central idea is to build a binary tree in which every leaf represents a symbol. The path from the root to a leaf determines its code: for example, left can represent 0 and right can represent 1.

compression.title: Compression process
compression.frequenciesCopy: The input file is read and each character occurrence is counted. For byte-based text, an array of 256 positions can be used.
compression.treeCopy: Each symbol with a positive frequency is inserted into a priority queue. The two nodes with the lowest frequency are extracted, combined into a parent, and the result is reinserted. The process ends when only one node remains: the root.
compression.tableCopy: The tree is traversed recursively. Every descent to the left adds a 0; every descent to the right adds a 1. Upon reaching a leaf, the accumulated bitfield is the character's code.
compression.localCopies: Local copies: each branch receives its own copy of the bitfield. It is simpler and safer.
compression.inPlace: In-place modification: the same object is modified and the last bit is removed when returning from recursion. It saves copies but requires more care.
compression.encodeCopy: Once the table is generated, the file is read again. Each character is replaced with its bit sequence and written to the compressed stream together with the information required to reconstruct the tree.
compression.removeCopy: When in-place modification is used, a function such as bits_remove_last makes it possible to go back one step along the tree path.

decompression.title: Decompression process
decompression.rebuildCopy: The decompressor reads the tree representation stored in the compressed file. A preorder traversal is usually used to distinguish internal nodes from leaves.
decompression.decodeCopy: With the tree rebuilt, bits are read one by one. A 0 moves the cursor left and a 1 right. Upon reaching a leaf, the character is written and the cursor returns to the root.
